transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-10
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: James Porter (Redwood AE), Lina Chen (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (CTO, Midtown Health), Rachel Kim (Head of Platform), Daniel Ortiz (Security Lead), Alyssa Moore (DevOps)

Summary:
Quick product walkthrough focused on rate limiting, quotas, and multi-tenant controls (org and project API keys). Customer is evaluating hosted Redwood API vs Dedicated/Private for regulated workflows; primary concerns are strong multi-tenant isolation, per-project quotas for internal teams, SSO/SAML + RBAC, and auditability for compliance. SE demo of console and API behaviors; discussed retry semantics and billing impacts. Agreed PoC and benchmark next steps.

Topics:
- Org vs project API keys and typical patterns
- Per-key rate limits / token bucket behavior and burst policies
- Console UI for quotas, per-route dashboards, and alerts
- Billing/usage reporting and how quotas affect spend
- Security: SAML/SSO, RBAC, KMS, audit logs, data residency
- PoC scope: perf benchmark and quota tuning

Transcript:
[00:00] James (Redwood): All right hey everyone thanks for making time, i'm James from Redwood, i'll kick off quick intro then Lina will do the demo.
[00:06] Samir (CTO): Hey James, thanks. we're excited — we've got a big push to standardize how engineering teams call LLMs, lots of internal projects.
[00:12] Rachel (Platform): yep we want per-team project keys and budgets so teams can't blow budgets, and strong audit logs.
[00:20] James: totally. today Lina will show org/project keys, rate limits, console quotas and how that ties to billing and alerts. sound good?
[00:26] Alyssa (DevOps): yes, also curious about SSO and service account rotation.
[00:30] Lina (SE): great, i'll share screen — sorry audio's a bit rough on my end — ok pulling up the Redwood Console.
[00:38] Lina: so here's the org view, you can see org-level settings, then projects underneath — each project gets its own set of API keys, quota windows, and rate limit overrides.
[00:48] Rachel: when you say "project" is that logical teams only or can we map to biz units?
[00:52] Lina: flexible — customers map projects however they like: team, product, client. keys are scoped to a project so usage attribution + billing are per-project.
[01:00] Daniel (Security): how do you handle key rotation and SSO? we need SAML and short-lived tokens ideally.
[01:06] James: good question — SSO via SAML/SCIM for user provisioning, and for API keys we support rotating keys and issuing short-lived service tokens via our private deployments/STS pattern; Lina will show some options.
[01:15] Lina: right — in the console here we can generate org keys (for admin-level operations) and project keys (for app-level). You can enforce key policies: TTL, required owner, metadata tags, and automatic rotation.
[01:30] Samir: do project keys have per-key rate limits? or is it only per-org?
[01:34] Lina: both. there are hierarchical policies: global org defaults, project overrides, and per-key overrides. rate-limiting uses a token-bucket model — you set steady qps and burst capacity.
[01:44] Samir: token bucket — so bursts are allowed but limited, how do you avoid noisy neighbors?
[01:50] Lina: we recommend per-project steady quotas for fairness, plus per-route limits for heavy endpoints. We also support enforcement tiers: soft-limit (warn + throttle) and hard-limit (429). For Dedicated customers you can pin capacity to projects to limit noisy neighbor effects.
[02:03] Rachel: show example?
[02:06] Lina: sure i’ll switch to policy editor — here i set org default 100 qps, burst 500 for 60s window, project A override 50 qps, burst 200. if a single API key exceeds project limit it gets 429 with Retry-After header.
[02:24] Speaker 1: (inaudible) is there backpressure to clients?
[02:28] Lina: yes we emit standard HTTP 429 and a Retry-After header. SDKs have built-in retry patterns and exponential backoff we recommend. Also we expose rate-limit headers in responses so clients can adapt.
[02:39] Alyssa: what about concurrency - we do a lot of streaming responses. does rate limit apply per-stream or per-token?
[02:46] Lina: rate limits are per-request QPS; streaming still counts as a request but we also have per-token metrics for billing; for latency sensitive streams we recommend a higher qps allocation or dedicated pool.
[02:58] James: also, we have KV cache + prefix caching to reduce cost and QPS for repeated prompts — can be helpful for bursty workloads.
[03:06] Samir: ok curious about quotas vs rate limits — we want monthly budgets for each project that can't be exceeded. how does that interact with rate limits?
[03:14] Lina: quotas are budget windows (daily/monthly token quotas) and operate independently of QPS rate limits. once a project exhausts its monthly tokens we can either block (hard stop), soft-stop with notification, or route to a cheaper model variant automatically.
[03:27] Rachel: routing to cheaper model variant is interesting — is that automatic? can we define fallback policies?
[03:32] Lina: yes you can create routing policies: e.g., if primary model hits capacity or quota, route to a quantized variant. Fallbacks can be per-project. That helps control spend without breaking service.
[03:44] Daniel: audit logs — we need per-request logs with key and project mapping, and export to our SIEM (Splunk).
[03:50] Lina: we stream audit logs to S3/Kafka and support direct integrations like Splunk and Datadog. logs include API key identifier, user id if available (via SAML), model, prompt hash — we can redact prompt contents at rest for PII.
[04:03] Samir: prompt hashing is good. can we configure redaction rules?
[04:06] Lina: yes you can choose full redact, partial, or none; defaults for enterprise are partial redact plus a retention policy you choose.
[04:14] James: also want to call out encryption and KMS — we support customer-managed keys (CMK) for private deployments and hosted options with KMS integration.
[04:23] Daniel: do hosted tenants get CMK?
[04:26] James: hosted customers can opt-in to a BYOK flow in our enterprise plans; Private gives full control.
[04:31] Rachel: on quotas, can we set budget alerts to slack channels and escalate to SRE?
[04:35] Lina: yes alerts are configurable by threshold, and we support webhook, email, and Slack. You can also create automatic workflows to open tickets.
[04:45] Alyssa: technical deep-dive — what happens under load when many project keys spike? you mentioned Dedicated pinned pools — explain more.
[04:53] Lina: sure — on hosted we have shared pools with smart routing and KV cache to absorb bursts. if you need guaranteed throughput you reserve Dedicated capacity — GPU pools pinned for your org. within Dedicated, projects get slices of that capacity so other orgs or projects don't affect you.
[05:06] Samir: good. for our regulated workflows we might want Dedicated or Private. can rate limits be enforced in Private as well?
[05:12] Lina: yes all policy engines run in Private deployments. you get the same console and APIs; enforcement happens locally.
[05:19] Speaker 2 (inaudible): how are quotas charged - is it tokens, requests, or seats?
[05:23] James: billing is primarily token-based with add-ons; quotas operate on token consumption but you can also set request-based thresholds. pricing details i'll share after the call.
[05:31] Rachel: do you have per-route dashboards? we need to see hot endpoints.
[05:35] Lina: yep per-route and per-model dashboards, latency and cost-per-route, error rates, and per-key breakdowns. here's a live demo of the dashboards — (screen) — you can filter by project, key, or model.
[05:50] Lina: show alert history — and you can link a policy to an alert to auto-scale a project or raise an ops ticket.
[05:58] Samir: can we limit which projects can call which models? e.g., only a few teams should be able to call a high-cost model.
[06:05] Lina: model-level access control is supported — RBAC roles combined with key-scoping. you can restrict model catalog access per project or role.
[06:13] Daniel: SAML integration specifics - do you map SAML groups to RBAC roles?
[06:17] James: yes SCIM + SAML mapping to roles. we can map groups to admin/owner/developer roles and bind to projects.
[06:24] Rachel: any guardrails for runaway prompts — e.g., a generated loop consuming tokens?
[06:29] Lina: we have token caps per-request and per-session, and policy engine can kill long-running sessions. Also can set up usage thresholds to send immediate alerts.
[06:39] Samir: nice. about 429s and client behavior, what do you recommend for SDKs?
[06:43] Lina: SDKs include retry helper that reads Retry-After and uses jitter backoff. for streaming we recommend checkpointing and resumable streams where needed.
[06:52] Alyssa: pow- we (sic) use k6 to run load tests. can you share a test harness or script?
[06:56] Lina: yes we have a PoC harness and a benchmark spreadsheet. i'll attach that.
[07:00] James: we'll add you to a shared folder after the call.
[07:04] Samir: on policy enforcement, is there a difference between throttling and dropping?
[07:09] Lina: throttling reduces allowed qps; dropping returns 429s immediately. we also have circuit-breaker patterns where after sustained errors we can switch to fallback routes.
[07:19] Rachel: how do quotas show up in billing UX? we need finance to map spend to projects.
[07:24] Lina: billing exports include per-project token usage and cost. you can export to CSV or push to billing systems. we also have monthly budget alerts.
[07:33] Daniel: audit retention periods and compliance — SOC2 type II evidence?
[07:37] James: we publish SOC2 report for hosted customers and we can provide an audit pack for enterprise, and Private deployments enable air-gapped evidence. we'll send SOC2 and penetration test summaries.
[07:49] Speaker 3: (someone typing) are there throttles for embeddings endpoints? they're heavy.
[07:53] Lina: embeddings can have their own rate limits and quotas. you can set them per-model or per-route — often teams put lower qps for embeddings and use async batching.
[08:03] Samir: any multi-tenant pitfalls you typically see?
[08:07] Lina: common ones: relying only on org-level limits (no project isolates), not using per-route limits, and failing to set budget alerts. recommend default per-project quotas and alerting.
[08:17] Alyssa: latency SLOs - if a project uses more than allocated qps and we throttle, our app SLA could be affected. we need graceful degradation options.
[08:25] Lina: you can configure graceful degradation: route to a cheaper fallback model, return cached responses for repeated prompts, or degrade to non-LLM flow.
[08:35] Rachel: about org vs project keys, is it possible to have service accounts that act across projects?
[08:40] James: yes service accounts can be granted cross-project roles; it's explicit binding. we advise least privilege.
[08:47] Samir: what about inter-team billing splits? can we automatically allocate shared capacity cost?
[08:52] Lina: we support tags and cost allocation rules to split invoices; you can attribute shared capacity by percentage or usage.
[08:59] Daniel: encryption in transit and at rest — standard TLS, and CMEK for at-rest?
[09:03] James: yes TLS for transit, CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) supported for hosted enterprise and full control in Private.
[09:12] Rachel: let's talk about PoC timeline — we'd like to start early Jan, run 2 weeks of synthetic load and one week of integration.
[09:18] James: sounds good. Lina will coordinate benchmarks and we'll send the test harness.
[09:22] Lina: i'll follow up with the k6 scripts and a preconfigured dataset.
[09:27] Samir: about rate-limit headers — what fields do you return? we need remaining quota per-minute and reset time.
[09:33] Lina: we return X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset and a Retry-After on 429. Also we attach project id and key id in logs.
[09:44] Alyssa: do you have SDK support for rotating a key midstream? how disruptive?
[09:49] Lina: rotating keys is seamless if you issue a new key and update clients; we support key aliases so you can switch without changing code, plus overlap windows for rotation.
[09:59] Samir: what about throttling granularity — do you support per-endpoint bursts?
[10:03] Lina: yes per-route burst windows are supported; you can set different token buckets per endpoint.
[10:12] Rachel: competitor question — some vendors charge per-request which makes quotas messy. how do you compare?
[10:17] James: our model is token-first which maps more directly to cost; we provide both token quotas and request quotas to match customer needs.
[10:25] Speaker 1: (murmur) any limits on number of projects?
[10:29] Lina: scales to thousands of projects; console can filter and group.
[10:33] Daniel: security review next steps — we'll want a formal design doc and threat model from you.
[10:38] James: we'll include a security whitepaper and post a design doc summarizing policies.
[10:42] Samir: ok good. action items?
[10:45] James: recap — Lina will send PoC harness and benchmark script, i'll send pricing and SOC2/SAML docs, Samir will confirm PoC stakeholders and timeline.
[10:55] Rachel: can we get a sample policy config to review?
[10:58] Lina: yes i'll export a sample policy repo with org defaults and project overrides.
[11:02] Samir: perfect. any outstanding blockers?
[11:05] Daniel: just internal approvals for data residency — we may need Private for PHI workloads.
[11:10] James: understood, we'll include Private deployment notes and migration path for PHI.
[11:14] Alyssa: thanks folks — curious in PoC we'll test scaling to 2k qps per-project, hope that's doable.
[11:20] Lina: for hosted we might need Dedicated for guaranteed 2k qps; we'll size that in proposal.
[11:26] Samir: great.
[11:28] James: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with docs and schedule the PoC kickoff for early January.
[11:35] Rachel: thanks all.

(End of recording)
